Subject: PulseHealth post-demo: stakeholder list + next steps

Kimberly — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and questions from our side: 

- Stakeholders we have lined up internally: Sarah Miles (CTO), Marco Diaz (VP Product), Priya Suresh (Head of Procurement), Nadia Flores (Legal counsel, cc'd), and Ethan (security contact, cc'd).
- Decision criteria: latency under 120ms for interactive flows, per-token cost guidance, data residency options (we prefer US-only for now), and SOC2 evidence.
- Procurement timeline: Procurement and legal want a mutual action plan; target to be under contract before 2027-01-15 if possible.

Two asks from procurement/legal/security: 
1) Can Redwood meet a 99.9% availability SLA with a financial credit for breach? Procurement indicated that a 99.9% SLA is preferred.
2) We're also asking if you can provide a one-time pilot discount or credit for the first quarter while we validate production load.

Next steps we propose:
- Kimberly introduces Sales Engineering and Sales Ops to our procurement team.
- Redwood to share a SOW draft and your security questionnaire (SOC2 summary).
- We will confirm the economic buyer by EOD tomorrow.

Happy to jump on a short call with procurement/legal if helpful.

Best,
Avery Collins
Head of Integrations, PulseHealth

- SLA: I will escalate the 99.9% SLA request to Sales Ops and Ben for approval; it is outside standard hosted terms but we can often do a variance with a conditional credit. I need to know the target RTO/RPO expectations and whether you require stricter regional commitments.
- Pilot credit: If PulseHealth can commit to a small reserved minimum for Q1 we typically provide a one-time onboarding credit; I will propose an introductory credit in the approval ask.

1) Today/Tomorrow: PulseHealth confirms economic buyer (you mentioned Sarah or Marco).
2) 12/1: Internal approvals for SLA/credit variance (I'll kick that off).

4) Week of 12/6: Procurement/legal review; DocuSign prep if accepted.

Ben / Dev — forwarding the PulseHealth recap (below). Key context and ask:

Deal: PulseHealth Analytics (DEAL-92814) — expected 12-month ARR if converted ~ $120k; pilot expected to include ~10M tokens over 6 weeks.
Timeline: Procurement aims to sign by 2027-01-15.
Key asks from customer:
- SLA: 99.9% availability commitment (hosted API) with a service credit schedule if breached.
- Pilot: one-time onboarding credit or 25% credit for first billing period while they validate load.
- Security: SOC2 summary + short security Q (attached security-questions.pdf).

Why I recommend approving:
- Strategic fit in health vertical; referenceable use-case (data flow + embeddings).
- Deal size justifies an exception if we keep the credit/timeboxed and require reserved minimum post-pilot.

Suggested approval terms (draft for Sales Ops):
- SLA: grant a 99.9% availability variance for 12 months, with a 10% invoice credit for any month where availability < 99.9% (cap at one month credit per year).
- Pilot credit: one-time 25% credit on first invoice, conditional on customer committing to a 3-month reserved minimum if they proceed to production within 90 days.

Attachments: SOW_draft_v2.pdf, security-questions.pdf

Can you confirm if Sales Ops can approve those terms, or if this needs Legal sign-off? Fast turnaround requested — procurement timeline is tight.

Thanks,
Kimberly
